subject: SlateProof: capacity validation & cutover ops
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SlateProof: capacity validation & cutover ops

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Per our conversation, putting the proposed validation & cutover ops in writing so we can align procurement and your infra team. High-level asks and timeline below: 

1) Target commit: 10 dedicated GPUs (H100 80GB equiv) initially, with an option to scale to 18 within 60 days after go-live.
2) Validation window (smoke + throughput): 48 hours of mirrored traffic, then a 24-hour soak with synthetic QPS to validate tail latency under 95th pct SLO.
3) Cutover blackout: 2-hour primary switchover window (UTC 02:00–04:00) with a 1-hour rollback guard.
4) Key pass/fail metrics: 95th pct token latency <= 120ms, throughput sustaining 1,200 rps steady-state (avg request size ~450 tokens).

Attached: commitment-schedule.xlsx (proposed fleet commit timeline) and SLA-diff.pdf (difference doc vs standard enterprise SLA).

Can you confirm: (a) procurement sign-off cadence, (b) whether your infra team can support traffic mirroring for the 48h smoke, and (c) any blackout windows we need to avoid?

I'll loop in Ben and Karthik as ops and capacity owners — they will run the smoke plan and sizing attestation.

Cheers,

Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference

> - Procurement: we can have an LOI by 10/25 but the legal review will likely take two weeks after LOI.
> - Mirroring: our infra team can mirror traffic, but they need the exact endpoints and a dry-run prior to the 48h window.

Thanks Emma — quick notes from ops: 

1) Mirror consumer: Redwood can provide a mirror consumer host inside our test VPC (TLS + signed tokens). We'll send a short runbook for request signing and a puppet script to stream a sanitized subset of traffic.
2) Expected mirrored footprint: during the 48h smoke we expect ~30% additional GPU token-processing compared to production due to duplication and instrumentation. For 10 H100 equiv that maps to roughly 3.5 additional GPU-hours per hour of mirrored traffic. We'll provide a cost estimate and can apply transient credits for the 48h window.
3) Staging fidelity tests: we recommend a 6-hour functional run in staging (shared dataset) before the mirrored smoke to catch prompt-parsing regressions. We can keep the dataset within your boundaries and sign an NDA addendum if needed.

Proposed initial dates: staging functional run — 2026-10-28 08:00–14:00 PDT; mirrored smoke — 2026-11-02 00:00–48:00 UTC window (flexible). Cutover target: 2026-11-05 02:00–04:00 UTC.

Ben / Grace: can you confirm runbook readiness and whether we need a warm standby fleet for extra headroom during the soak?

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Lead, Dedicated Capacity Ops, Redwood Inference

On Mon, Oct 19, 2026 at 08:04 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Proposed initial dates: staging functional run — 2026-10-28 08:00–14:00 PDT; mirrored smoke — 2026-11-02 00:00–48:00 UTC window (flexible). Cutover target: 2026-11-05 02:00–04:00 UTC.

All good from my side. A few operational details to call out so the PaperHealth SREs have clear expectations: 

- Warm standby: We'll provision a 20% warm standby cushion on day-of soak (i.e., 12 H100-equivalent reserved for the soak) to reduce risk of throttling while still meeting unit economics goals.
- KV/prefix cache: we'll enable an aggressive prefix KV cache for identical prompt families during the soak — this will lower token compute by ~18% for repeat prompts (we'll document the cache TTL).
- Rollback plan: if 95th pct latency exceeds 140ms for two consecutive 15-minute buckets OR error rate >1.5%, we will initiate rollback. Rollback path: DNS cut -> traffic re-route -> capacity release. Expected rollback execution time target: < 22 minutes.

Grace will own the post-smoke perf attestation doc and will share the template tomorrow.

Ben Carter
Director, Capacity Engineering, Redwood Inference
